what: GLM-5.3-Flash decode kernels. Every dimension is a metadata key from the model's own GGUF, read on 2026-11-02 -- none is chosen and none is inferred from a tensor shape.

shapes.ATTN_S_source: index_topk from zai-org/GLM-5.3 config.json; the DSA sparse attention window

shapes_source: the GLM-5.3-Flash-Q2 GGUF's own metadata keys (`glm5-next.*`), read with the engine's metadata dumper on 2026-11-02. Every value below is a key from that file, not a tensor-shape inference and not a choice.
architecture_note: `glm5-next` is a hybrid and the corpus reflects it: 34 of 46 blocks use a gated delta net, 12 use MLA, 43 FFNs are a 288-expert MoE and 3 are dense, and there is NO RoPE (rope_dimension_count = 0). This is a different architecture from GLM-5.2's `glm-dsa`, which is why the engine path that reads `glm-dsa.*` keys cannot load this model.

not_in_this_corpus.kda_recurrence: the delta-net state update -- a sequential scan with a decay term. The tile API has no recurrent-scan intrinsic: every op in it is a whole-tile map or reduction, and a scan is neither.
not_in_this_corpus.kda_short_conv: the depthwise causal convolution over 4 timesteps. The tile API has no sliding-window intrinsic, and expressing it as a matmul would change the arithmetic and the memory traffic both.
not_in_this_corpus.why_omitted: Approximating either would put a kernel in this corpus that computes something the model does not. Two thirds of this model's blocks use them, so the corpus covers the parts that are expressible and says plainly that it does not cover the rest.

representations.tile: generated by bench/shapes/gen_glm_5_3.py from the registry's sourced shapes.
representations.pto: from the in-tree rspto. Reproducible; a test asserts it byte for byte.
representations.tile-rs: Rust source against the tile intrinsics, lifted from the .pto by the in-tree ptoas-rs. COMPILED: a test checks every file in this column against the kernel-side DSL, and a second test checks that the lift still accepts the .pto it came from. Two of the eight kernels are here; the other six are refused by the lift for reasons its own census names.
representations.searched: for a refused kernel, the tiling tile-search chose instead.

argmax_glm53_1x154880.pto_refused: NPU tile bound (arch a2a3): row_major data tile cols=19360 * 4B = 77440B spans multiple 512B fractals with bad stride (C2); pad cols so cols*sizeof(dtype) % 512 == 0
argmax_glm53_1x154880.ascendc_refused_retracted_2026_11_08: RETRACTED: the bound was real and the arm did not exist. mlir_to_cpp now has a CHUNKED ARGMAX arm, the fourth rescue and the one the others cannot do -- an argmax carries a PAIR, a running maximum and the index that attained it, and the index's meaning depends on where its chunk started, so neither a tile accumulator nor a wider buffer helps. The emitted argmax block already computes exactly the per-chunk partial needed (ReduceMax for the value, one scalar pass for the first index attaining it), so the arm runs it verbatim per chunk (20 x 7744) and adds a pairwise reduce with the chunk base added back. Was: UB overflow in kernel 'glm53_argmax_154880': buffer 0 needs 154880 elements (619520 bytes), which is larger than the ENTIRE 188416 byte unified buffer. No division of the budget can hold this tile -- it has to be streamed from global memory in chunks, and mlir_to_cpp has no blocked path for this ope
argmax_glm53_1x154880.ascendc_index_is_typed_now: The same change retired this kernel's TILE_SUBSTITUTION. Its .tile declared __tile_store_f32 for an argmax INDEX, so the AscendC arm had to write `replacement=f32-index-storage; reason=u32-buffer-typing-unavailable` -- a marker about a choice the emitter never made, since the source asked for the f32. The generator now declares __tile_store_i32, mlir_to_cpp has that store (it already existed in mlir_to_pto), and the index buffer is typed int32_t, so the store arm's dtype check enforces the pair instead of a comment describing it. Under the migration campaign's eligibility clause the marker capped this kernel at `tiled` whatever a device run said; there is now nothing to cap.
argmax_glm53_1x154880.device_check: PASS 2026-11-08 on 910B2 (CANN 8.5.2 aarch64, dav-2201), ORACLE 41 (argmax index, tie policy = lowest index attaining the maximum), n=154880, two identical runs: want=51626 got=51626 EXACT, max=1.000000e+03, ties=2, position=0.333 of n. The POSITION and TIES figures are the evidence that the chunked carry was exercised rather than bypassed: the maximum sits in chunk 6 of 20, so a kernel that forgot the chunk base would have returned 5162, and the deliberate second maximum at 2n/3 means a carry using >= instead of > would have returned 103253. Both are refuted, not merely unobserved.

embedding_glm53_154880x4096.pto_refusal_retracted_2026_11_10: RETRACTED: the op existed and the ARM did not. The old text read -- mlir_to_pto has no arm for `__tile_get_value_f32`. The kernel is a GM row copy and the scalar read-back is the one step this emitter cannot take; the AscendC column carries it. Emitting it anyway would drop the operation silently. -- and its premise, that the scalar read-back is a step this emitter cannot take, was about the emitter and read as if it were about PTO. `ptoas` ships as a Python package, so its op registry is inspectable, and `ptoas/mlir/dialects/_pto_ops_gen.py:22306` has declared `pto.tgetval(src, offset) -> value` all along. It never appears in the corpus's .pto vocabulary because nothing had emitted it -- scraping the corpus for the dialect's ops is a narrowing query, and it returned a plausible absence. mlir_to_pto now has arms for `__tile_get_value_f32` -> `pto.tgetval` and `__tile_load_at_f32` -> a runtime-offset `partition_view`, plus `llvm.mul` on a runtime scalar -> `arith.muli`. Operand and result types were MEASURED, not inferred: of five plausible spellings exactly one assembles (offset `index`, result `f32`). The offset is converted to an integer BEFORE the multiply, so unlike the AscendC path it carries no float-exactness bound on the row width. Inertness: 75 of 75 pre-existing .pto regenerate byte-identically, 0 changed.
embedding_glm53_154880x4096.ascendc_refused_retracted_2026_11_08: RETRACTED 2026-11-08: the bound was real and the LOWERING was wrong. `__tile_embedding_f32` declares its weight table as a tile, so no arm can satisfy it at vocabulary scale -- but the operation does not need that intrinsic. At decode shape it is one row copy from GM: read the index, multiply by the row width, `__tile_load_at_f32` at that element offset. The generator now emits that form and this emitter takes it, with the offset reaching the generated `DataCopy(buf1, gm0Tensor[__v3], ...)` so the table is never resident. Kept rather than deleted so the refusal that licensed `ascendc: null` also records its retirement. Was: UB overflow: `__tile_embedding_f32` gathers rows from a tile that holds `dim` element(s) while the vocabulary needs `vocab * dim`. The table cannot be resident, so its rows must be copied from global memory one at a time, and `mlir_to_cpp` has no GM-driven embedding path.

router_topk_glm53_1x288_k8.device_check_not_covered: The k VALUES through gm1. This kernel has two outputs and at KERNEL_ARGS == 3 the harness copies back gm2 alone, so the indices are compared and the value store is not. The indices identify the selection completely and the value written is the same one the index was found for, so what is unchecked is whether it reached the right slot of the other buffer. Widening the copy-back would overwrite `b`, which several existing oracles read as an INPUT, so it is not a change an added oracle may make. The oracle PRINTS this line on every run rather than leaving it to be discovered.

routed_gate_up_glm53_8x2048.tile_rs_refused_retracted_2026_11_09: RETRACTED: the bound was not real. The old text read -- refused bench/glm_5_3/pto/routed_gate_up_glm53_8x2048.pto: partition view `%pto1_u0` is a 8x512 window of a 8x2048 parent; its rows are 2048 elements apart in memory while the tile call reads 4096 contiguous ones, so the lift would read past each row -- and the premise in its last clause was false: the tile call need not read contiguously. tile_std exports tile_load_strided_f32<ROWS, COLS, ROW_STRIDE> and tile_store_strided_f32 (crates/tile_std/src/tile.rs:1592,:1603), which take exactly this geometry. The lift discarded the parent's row stride in windows.rs before any emitter arm could ask for it, so the refusal described the lift's own data loss as a hardware constraint. Window now carries strided: Option<(cols, row_stride)> and len is the reach (rows-1)*parent_cols + cols. Lifted output: 8x512 tiles, four unrolled chunks at offsets 0/512/1024/1536 covering the 2048-wide row exactly; rustc accepts it. Evidence: campaign evidence/0031-strided-partition-windows/.

tile_rs_removed_2026_11_02.why: They did not compile, and the lift can no longer produce them. Each stored a 1x1 reduce result through `tile_store_f32::<8, 1>` -- `expected 8, found 1` -- because the emitter read a tile_buf's `rows`/`cols`, the extent ALLOCATED against the 512-byte fractal, where `v_row`/`v_col` carries the logical shape. The lift now refuses those `.pto` artifacts by name ('tile `%pto8` has a partial or dynamic v_row'), so these files are output of a generator that no longer exists in that form. Found by compiling the corpus for the first time, which only became possible when the kernel-side DSL was carried into this tree.
tile_rs_removed_2026_11_02.to_restore: Thread the valid extent through the emitter instead of the allocated one, then prove on hardware that the store writes one element and not eight. Until that is measured, a refusal is worth more than a kernel that compiles and writes the wrong count.

estimated_decode_kernels.source: derived from the model's own configuration by inventory(); a LOWER BOUND, because the inventory predicted 15 for DeepSeek V4 Flash against a registry count of 52, so it under-counts by about 3.5x. Not applied as a correction: one anchor cannot calibrate a model, and a derivation multiplied by 3.5 would look measured and would not be.
estimated_decode_kernels.what_it_is: The number of distinct kernels one decode step of this model needs -- the denominator the representation counts are read against. Where the count is KNOWN it is used; where it is not, inventory() derives a LOWER BOUND from the model's own configuration. Not a measurement of a running engine in either case.
estimated_decode_kernels.derivation_error: the inventory predicted 15 for DeepSeek V4 Flash against a registry count of 52, so it under-counts by about 3.5x. Not applied as a correction: one anchor cannot calibrate a model, and a derivation multiplied by 3.5 would look measured and would not be.
estimated_decode_kernels.a_kernel_is: one distinct (operation, shape) pair, because that is what this corpus holds -- one rmsnorm file serves every block that shares D. A layer count does not multiply it.

inventory.line: rmsnorm at D (attn_norm, ffn_norm and the final norm share it)
MLA projections: q_a, q_b, kv_a, kv_b, output
second attention core: the gated delta net
routed expert gate/up at MOE_INTER, and down at D
the leading dense blocks' gate/up at DENSE_FFN_INTER, and down at D

estimated_decode_kernels.reconciliation: 15 kernels present + the rows named above = the DERIVED inventory total of 20. It does not reconcile against 20 when that is a lower bound from another source, and it is not meant to: the gaps were enumerated against the inventory.

what_the_inventory_collapses.each expert's gate, up and down are one: a real engine has three kernels there, and the gate/up pair is often fused separately from the down-projection
what_the_inventory_collapses.one attention core: decode, prefill and partial/chunked are different kernels with different shapes, and a model with two attention types doubles that again
what_the_inventory_collapses.one matvec per projection: f16 and f32 weight forms are separate kernels, and each quantisation the engine supports adds another (q8_0, q4_K, iq2_xxs, mxfp4 ...)
what_the_inventory_collapses.no prefill shapes: every projection and norm has a batched prefill form, which is a different kernel from its decode form
what_the_inventory_collapses.no quantise/dequantise kernels: activation quantisation and weight unpacking are real kernels; the inventory treats weight format as out of scope
what_the_inventory_collapses.one sampling kernel: argmax is counted; top-p, top-k sampling and draft verification are not

estimated_decode_kernels.why_collapses_are_listed_not_multiplied: 'under-counts by 3.5x' is one number and tells a reader nothing they can act on. These name the specific rows that each stand for several real kernels. They are not multiplied out: that would turn a list of known omissions into a fabricated total. Someone who knows the true count for this model can see which rows to expand.
estimated_decode_kernels.published_registry: the published kernel registry, read 2026-11-02, holds 6 distinct kernels for this model, all of them model-prefixed and all under a `source-scan` basis. That is FEWER than this manifest's derived lower bound, and the registry was generated 2026-08-31, before this architecture's work landed. The derived bound therefore stands: adopting a smaller external figure would lower a bound on the strength of its provenance alone. The 6 is recorded as a floor on model-specific kernels alone.
estimated_decode_kernels.note: 27 since 2026-11-06: the seven KDA projections (kda_q/k/v 8192 out from k=4096, f_a/g_a 128 out, f_b/g_b 8192 out from k=128) are real tensors in the model's own file and were missing from the estimate. They could not be emitted before iteration 151 because the w8a8 arm faulted above ~1280 outputs at k=4096 -- the estimate was low because the TOOL was limited, not because the model was smaller.
estimated_decode_kernels.verify_args_convention: From 2026-11-06 every certified kernel records `verify_args`: the args column of its verify_all.sh row. `sync_verify_all.py` derives missing rows from it, because four rounds committed with a red gate from adding that row by hand.
